Sophia M: quick heads-up — rerank eval suite shows a reproducible NDCG regression when using the int8 quantized build for new-llm-v2q. float32 and q8im8 (old path) match, but our latest qint8 path produces reversed order for 6/1k queries. attaching minimal repro below.

Jon K: ugh, do you have a tiny failing example we can run locally? is it consistent across seeds or only CI? :thinking:

Sophia M: it's consistent across seeds and on my laptop (mac m1 + docker). here's a trimmed example where similarity order flips after quant:

```
# toy repro (numpy pseudo)
a = np.array([0.312, -0.042, 0.0012, 0.11])
b = np.array([0.201, 0.003, -0.002, -0.09])
# float dot
float_dot = a.dot(b)  # ~0.049
# quant (symmetric int8 with scale = max(abs(vec))/127)
a_q = (a / 0.003).round().astype(np.int8)
b_q = (b / 0.003).round().astype(np.int8)
int_dot = (a_q.astype(int) * b_q.astype(int)).sum() * (0.003**2)
```

Mateo R: interesting — that looks like rounding + saturation could flip small negative components. did we accidentally switch to asymmetric quant (with a nonzero zero_point) in the new kernel? that would add a bias term.

Zhen L: quick check — our int8 kernel had an optimization that uses floor instead of round for speed. floor(x/scale) vs round can systematically bias small values toward negative. also we had an earlier bug where we failed to subtract zero_point when computing dequant for dot-product accumulation in the batched path.

eval-ci-bot: CI run rerank-suite/quant-ci #402 finished: FAIL (ndcg@10 drop -0.072, mrr drop -0.015). logs: https://ci/internal/402

Rachel P: also flagging that the eval harness normalization might be masking changes: we compute NDCG with normalization by ideal DCG for top-10, but the previous reference used top-100 denom for some datasets which reduces sensitivity to small swaps. which denom are you using for this run?

Sophia M: this run used topk=10 for both numerator and denom. i can re-run with topk=100 to see if magnitude shrinks — but the order flips for the examples above so even full-k should show change.

Jon K: ok next steps:
- Zhen: check quant path for floor vs round and the zero_point subtraction in batched accumulation (priority)
- Sophia: collect 10 minimal queries where order flips and post as json with embeddings (sanitized)
- Mateo: add a unit test that compares float vs dequantized int accumulation on small vectors (use both round and floor)
- Rachel: run rerank-suite with denom=k=100 to produce a sensitivity report

Zhen L: quick experiment confirmed — switching floor -> round removes the sign flips on repro vectors. failure was a combination: floor rounding + missing zero_point subtraction in the blocked GEMM path. PR incoming.

Sophia M: nice. can you link the PR? i'll re-run CI afterward.

Zhen L: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/quant-kernels/pull/817 — description + microbench. note: i kept the floor branch behind an env flag to avoid perf regressions until we validate.

eval-ci-bot: ci/presubmit #817 started (quant-kernels). job: unit-quant-tests, rerank-smoke

Mateo R: i added a test to our eval harness that runs float vs dequant accumulation on 1000 randomized small vectors and fails if any pair's cosine/sim sign flips. pushed as branch "embed-quant-signcheck".

Rachel P: for the dashboard, i'll add an alert when ndcg@10 delta > 0.03 and > 10 failing queries with order flip exceptions. also going to add a note in the report about denom differences so folks don't confuse metric magnitude changes for algorithmic flips.

Sophia M: thanks all — feel good about the fix path. after CI passes let's roll the quant build to canary and monitor ndcg/mrr on the test production traffic for 24h.

Jon K: heads-up for release notes: "fixed int8 quantization accumulation bug that caused sign flips in low-magnitude embedding coordinates leading to rerank order inversions". add to changelog under eng-ml.

Mateo R: small caveat — we should also audit any other kernels that used floor to be safe. i can scan the codebase for floor or trunc quant ops tomorrow.

Sophia M: perfect. tagging @everyone: please ack if you own one of the items above. :thumbsup:
